Subject: Renewal restructuring — fiscal alignment + staged capacity waterfall

Hi Sophie,

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our discussion I've put together a concise alternate renewal structure that aligns Redwood's contract boundary with Cloudfolio's fiscal calendar while giving you staged capacity increases over the first 12 months. The goal is to reduce month-to-month billing variance for you and keep the unit economics predictable as usage ramps.

High-level:
- 36-month master term, with first 12 months on a staggered ramp schedule (monthly increasing committed tokens).
- Optional automatic annual renewal (auto-roll) after year 1 unless procurement opts out with 60 days notice.
- Billing smoothing: invoices at co-term calendar boundaries with quarterly true-ups for overage.
- Early uplift credits: if you hit the tiered usage triggers, we'll apply a one-time onboarding credit to offset front-loaded utilization.

Attached is a one-page proposal and a playbook with the proposed ramp table and example invoice cadence (Redwood_Proposal_Cloudfolio_2026Q2.pdf; staggered_ramp_playbook.xlsx).

Can you review and flag any procurement/legal items we should preempt before we send an official amendment? If this looks directionally helpful, I'd like to schedule a short follow-up with Camila and Karthik on pricing/legal next week.

Best,
Lauren

Thanks for the context — drove a quick internal take and proposed edits below.

Summary of changes I recommend before we send to legal:
- Billing treatment: mark initial ramp months as applied usage credits (non-refundable), itemized on invoice as "Onboarding Ramp Credit" so finance can see the offset. That avoids Cash Refund language and simplifies accounting.
- Co-terming: we’ll generate a single co-term invoice at the fiscal quarter boundary (Apr 1) with a separate quarterly true-up line item. For partial periods we propose prorated true-ups rather than issuing micro invoices.
- Auto-roll: keep 60-day opt-out. Add explicit clauses: (i) auto-roll notice will be emailed to the procurement alias; (ii) auto-roll will be void if there is a >10% price increase or unresolved major security incident in previous 12 months.
- Credits: propose a one-time onboarding credit that is applied to the first invoice after the quarter boundary; credit amount tied to the percent uplift in month 3 vs. baseline.

Next steps: Camila — can you model the invoice examples (sample Q1 / Q2 mock invoice) and I’ll put together the legal redline (we should use our standard amendment template and highlight the new co-term/auto-roll sections). Lauren — if you can confirm the desired credit sizing (Sophie suggested it be modest, just to offset early burst), I’ll finalize language.

-Karthik
